heroes.name: The Severn
heroes.note: the tenement the poet looks for a way out of: hallways, drawers, fire escapes

facts.claim: a 2 m hallway runs the width of every floor: three flats in front, two behind, the stair at the back
fire escapes on the front, the way the shots show them
riser and tread meet a residential stair (≤ 0.2 m, ≥ 0.25 m)
two ways down from every flat: the stair and the fire escape
brick bearing walls carry 8 m floor spans
cast-iron columns carry the shopfront floors
every flat is ≤ 8 m deep between the hallway wall and the facade

fit.saw: the fire escape is one long diagonal flight across the brick between landings
fit.did: flights now run the width of the landing, stringers and rails, alternating left and right

fit.saw: windows sit in carved stone surrounds
fit.did: stone surrounds with a keystone on every outside window

fit.saw: the brick is lit red and teal at night, wet
fit.did: a red-and-teal night setting with coloured light raking the facade

fit.saw: a long hallway of doors (interior reference)
fit.did: the plan now turns on a long hallway of numbered doors, lamps every three metres, a runner, radiators

heroes.name: The chapel on the flat
heroes.note: the chapel the flood ruined; the Resurrection vaulted the white temple over its ruin

facts.claim: a dark stone nave, its bell on the front gable, alone on the tidal flat
the floor is raised 0.6 m above the flat (the stoop says so)
the 9 m nave spans on timber trusses
the Fall took the roof; the walls stood
the white temple is vaulted over the ruin, not on it

fit.saw: dark grey stone, not whitewash
fit.did: walls re-skinned in grey cantera

fit.saw: a steep pointed gable; the bell hangs in a bell-cote on the gable apex, not a tower
fit.did: roof raised to 5.6 m; a pierced bell-cote rises from the front gable past the ridge

fit.saw: tall pointed windows
fit.did: lancet arches on the nave and the narthex

fit.saw: it stands alone on a wet tidal flat under storm cloud, mirrored
fit.did: a tidal setting: wet reflecting sand, low storm light

fit.saw: inside, a shaft of light breaks into colour on a wet floor (interior reference)
fit.did: a shaft of light falls from a lancet onto a wet stone floor and breaks into colour; stained glass; open timber trusses to the roof

fit.saw: a tall pointed door in the front gable
fit.did: the street door is a 3.8 m lancet

fit.saw: the chapel is small in a wide, low frame; the flat and the sky carry it
fit.did: the hero shot pulled back to a 24° lens near the ground

heroes.name: The NEW SINGLE
heroes.note: the picture palace of Newly Single: a marquee from our own generated footage, made into a theatre you can walk into

rooms.name: lobby
props: NOW SHOWING · WHERE YOU GO WHEN YOU LEAVE

exterior.sub: TONIGHT · WHERE YOU GO WHEN YOU LEAVE

facts.claim: the marquee and its letters come from a frame in our generated footage
a 16 m auditorium spans on steel trusses
the projection booth sits over the lobby, throwing light the length of the house
one stair to the foyer; the auditorium exits straight to the street

fit.saw: a row of glowing poster boxes at street level, doubled in the wet street
fit.did: six lit poster cases flank the doors; a wet night street that reflects

fit.saw: a dark red corridor with benches (interior reference)

heroes.name: The pier café
heroes.note: the café at the root of the pier, striped awnings and the ship's masts behind

facts.claim: teal boards, white trim, striped awnings at the root of the pier
the café stands on the pier deck, 0.4 m up
every room has its own window

fit.saw: timber posts and beams over the terrace tables, canvas between
fit.did: a pergola over the 4 m terrace with a balustrade

fit.saw: the harbour and masts right behind

heroes.name: The clock tower
heroes.note: New Day: climb the stair to the room behind the clock faces

facts.claim: a brick shaft, a switchback stair, the clock room on top
the tower is not occupied: one stair is enough
the clock faces are the clock room's windows; you see the hands from behind

fit.saw: stepped buttresses at the corners
fit.did: three-stage buttresses on every corner

fit.saw: tall pointed windows on the shaft
fit.did: lancet windows on every shaft storey

fit.saw: a steep spire, taller than the shaft's width suggests
fit.did: pyramid raised to 8 m and a 14 m needle

fit.saw: gears, chain and the clock seen from behind (interior)

heroes.name: The Atlantis rowhouse
heroes.note: the everyday unit of the city: brick, a marble stoop, a dark middle room, an addition over the back porch

facts.claim: 5 m wide between party walls, windows only front and back
the middle room is dark; it borrows light from the kitchen through a 2 m opening
the back bedroom is the addition, cantilevered 1.5 m over the porch
a marble stoop climbs the 1 m to the raised parlour floor

fit.saw: a brownstone row: stoops climbing to raised doors, bays pushed out
fit.did: brownstone skin and a two-storey bay beside the stoop
